test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

(Left) 248 382 425 127 335 (Right)

(Example- 697 - First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

NOTE - All operations to be done from left to right.

If 3 is added to the first digit of every number, in how many numbers will the first digit be exactly divisible by the second digit?
solution:
Given: (left) 248 382 425 127 335 (right)

If 3 is added to the first digit of every number, we get the following numbers:

 
• 248: 2 + 3 = 5, so the new number is 548
 
• 382: 3 + 3 = 6, so the new number is 682
 
• 425: 4 + 3 = 7, so the new number is 725
 
• 127: 1 + 3 = 4, so the new number is 427
 
• 335: 3 + 3 = 6, so the new number is 635

Now, we check how many numbers have the first digit exactly divisible by the second digit:

 
• 548: 5 is not divisible by 4
 
• 682: 6 is not divisible by 8
 
• 725: 7 is not divisible by 2
 
• **427: 4 is divisible by 2**
 
• **635: 6 is divisible by 3**

So, there are 2 numbers where the first digit is exactly divisible by the second digit.

The correct answer is **Option 2**.
